games.description: TBC (2.4.3) on CMaNGOS with the CMaNGOS playerbots fork.

phases.name: instance updates
notes: tbc-db's InstallFullDB.sh applies Updates/Instances/[0-9]*.sql straight after Updates/[0-9]*.sql and before the world core updates, dbc data and ACID, stopping on the first error; this phase sits in that same place (T141). At ba4755de and at 86672361 that is 55 files, 000_setup.sql first, and this phase's natural order was measured equal to bash's glob order over them.

000_setup.sql deletes every creature and gameobject spawn on the instance maps from 36 tables and the files after it put them back, so the set is one rebuild and a failure part way leaves dungeons and raids short. It cannot be one transaction: the setup creates and drops real tables (DDL commits), and creature, gameobject, pool_template and most of the others are MyISAM in the Full_DB dump. So `fail`, which writes no marker, and the next press's `partial` arm drops the schemas and imports again.

Nothing in these files records that they ran: no db_version column, no ledger. New installs only, by the owner's decision of 2026-09-29: no `reapply_when_changed`, so a server imported before this phase existed reads it as withheld.

games.name: WoW Tortoise
games.description: Turtle WoW's world on the Tortoise core, the code the Turtle WoW V2 servers are built from, with the TortoiseBots bots built in. Yu'lon compiles it from source in Docker.
notes: Penqle core: tortoise-wow/tortoise-wow branch 1181dev, a MaNGOS Zero lineage, with the TortoiseBots module compiled in statically and the whole thing source-compiled in Docker.

1181dev is main plus the SOAP interface (PR #491, merged there 2026-09-17); it carries the headless bot sessions (PR #438, bot-helpers is fully merged into main) the bots module requires, and the bots themselves are Sagiroth/TortoiseBots, cloned into modules/TortoiseBots.
It replaces the retired Shyalya fork that vendored the cmangos playerbots; a server already installed from that fork goes on opening, starting and being played, and is not migrated.
Commands reach this world over SOAP again: the core builds gsoap from source behind ENABLE_SOAP, which the image template switches on (T86, 2026-09-17).
Installed, started and pressed headless through the app's own seams on the test box; no client rendered there (T30, T86).

phases.name: world base
notes: 190 per-table tw_world dumps on the pinned core, counted on yulon-arch 2026-09-11 (T30 Half 1, 06-sql-layout.txt). Unchanged from the retired fork.

THREE PHASES WERE REMOVED HERE, each naming a directory this tree does not have, all three read on the same day: `playerbots characters` and `playerbots world` globbed `modules/mod-playerbots/sql/...`, which went with the vendored cmangos playerbots, and `character updates` globbed `sql/character_updates/`, which the Penqle core has never had. The last of those was `on_error: fail`, so it would have stopped every fresh install on a directory that is simply absent.

NOTHING IN THIS PLAN IMPORTS THE BOTS' OWN SQL, and that is not an omission. The core's own updater applies module migrations at world start from `<TW_SOURCE_MODULES_DIR>/TortoiseBots/data/sql/<CharUpdateName|WorldUpdateName>` (`AutoUpdater.cpp:245-283`, `:497-531`) -- the same `character` and `world` folder names this entry's conf block writes. Measured on yulon-arch 2026-09-11: 5 character and 3 world module migrations applied at first start, and the ai_playerbot_* tables exist afterwards (Half 1 run 2, 08d/08e). The Dockerfile is what makes that compiled-in path resolve inside the runtime image; its comment says how and why.

The removed `character updates` was also the catalog's only `rerun_on_marked` phase (T11), so this plan has none. An install made from the retired fork keeps every row it already has -- that flag only ever ADDED a re-run -- and every glob this plan still carries resolves on that older tree too, so pressing Install on one refuses or proceeds by its marker exactly as before.

phases.name: character_inventory_copy table
statements: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `character_inventory_copy` LIKE `character_inventory`
notes: THE TABLE HONOR MAINTENANCE TRUNCATES, which nothing on the pinned core creates (T159). `HonorMaintenancer::DoMaintenance()` runs in `World::SetInitialWorldSettings()` on the first start after a running world has marked the week's honor day (`saved_variables.honorMaintenanceMarker`), and with `BackupCharacterInventory = 1` -- the dist conf's value, which this entry's conf block leaves alone -- it calls `ObjectMgr::BackupCharacterInventory()`: `TRUNCATE character_inventory_copy`, then `INSERT ... SELECT * FROM character_inventory` (`ObjectMgr.cpp:10123-10130`). Read at 187af788: no CREATE for it in `create_databases.sql`, `database_updates/` or TortoiseBots' `data/sql`. Errno 1146 there is `ASSERT(false)` in `HandleMySQLError` (`DatabaseMysql.cpp:185-191`), a throw nothing catches, and the marker is cleared only by a maintenance that finished -- so every restart dies on the same statement. Measured on the retired fork's identical C++ on 2026-09-09 (`.notes/gates/7.9-rerun-m910q-2026-09-09`, finding 1), where its `character_updates/20260812142512_character_inventory_copy.sql` was the file that made the table; that directory went with the fork.

`LIKE`, as that file had it: `INSERT ... SELECT *` needs the copy's columns to be the original's, and `LIKE` takes the engine and keys too (MyISAM, for `DISABLE KEYS`). `IF NOT EXISTS` keeps whatever a server made by hand, and makes the statement safe to apply to a server that already has data -- which is what `reapply_when_changed` offers it for: every Tortoise server a release installed is offered this one step, behind a dialog, on the Server tab. Also `.character diffitems` reads this table and dies the same way without it.

`same_columns` because `IF NOT EXISTS` is also what lets a WRONG table through: a copy somebody made by hand with other columns is left as it is, and the core's `INSERT ... SELECT *` then fails on it every week. So the step is recorded as landed only when the copy has `character_inventory`'s columns in order, alike in name, type, nullability, charset, collation and `extra`, and otherwise the press names the table and says to rename or drop it (Codex, T159).

Not `BackupCharacterInventory = 0` instead: that leaves `diffitems` on the same assert, turns off an upstream feature, and reaches an existing server only through an Install press, since a rebuild does not re-run the conf stage.

verify.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='tw_world'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='tw_char' AND table_name='character_inventory_copy'

patches.reason: tortoise-wow's DB auto-updater ends a failed migration with std::getline(std::cin) (src/shared/Database/AutoUpdater.cpp:236-239 at 187af788); the world container keeps stdin open for the Console tab, so the read never returns and a failed update hangs the world with no signal handler, no SOAP and no error line. The patch drops the read so the world reports the failure and exits, as Shyalya's fork did in b405b10adb

play.rename_offline_refusal: has to be logged in before a rename can be flagged on this server -- the same command run on an offline character here replaces the name with the character's guid instead, so it is not sent
play.set_level_absent_reason: This server can't move a character to a level you pick. From the Console it can reset a logged-in character to the starting level, or make a new bot at the level you name.

notes: SOAP IS BACK ON THIS CORE since PR #491 merged into 1181dev on 2026-09-17 (57abad6f3): ns1__executeCommand under urn:MaNGOS, HTTP Basic auth, SEC_ADMINISTRATOR (rank 4) required, banned accounts refused (403), the rank and the ban read from the row per request, 64 KiB request cap. The core's CMake option ENABLE_SOAP defaults OFF, so the image template passes -DENABLE_SOAP=ON; without it this block would install cleanly and answer nothing.

This block is the same one that stood here between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-11 (c7e577c7) and that T30's `attach` note kept as the way back; the transport in ui/controller_view.py `_for_tortoise` is channel_setup.InstallChannel over channel.SoapChannel again, and tests/test_catalog_operations.py expects `soap`.
Only the custom Turtle-WoW 1.18.1 client (build 7272) works; any other build will not connect.
